title: the method that runs is the one on the class the caller constructed, not the interface member the signature selected: a class instance argument is part of the pinned graph

xfail.reason: The fork accepts this program, grants the pin, and RUNS it. Measured 2026-08-23 through conformance/runner/backend-go.mjs: zero diagnostics, exit 0, stdout ["1"] — where the reference reports SMITHERS3001@18:1 with the route `... #pinned -> reader-callee.mod.sm#run -> ...#read`. Nothing else in the compile reports it, because `eval` is legal on its own and only the pin refuses it. This is the same missing question as 21-native-pin/a-callback-a-callee-invokes-is-part-of-the-pinned-graph in its other spelling: the fork walks the declaration the checker's signature resolution selected, and for `reader.read()` that is an INTERFACE MEMBER with no body, so the walk enters nothing. It does not then ask which VALUE arrived at the call, which is the question that reaches `Widener#read`. It is a missing walk and not a missing rule: the fork owns SMITHERS3001, owns the `TypeScript` classification of `eval` (21-native-pin/a-pin-reaching-typescript-is-rejected passes there), and charges `eval` through an immediately-invoked function expression and through a `Layer.provide` callback. What is unowned is the value question at a call whose signature has no body.
xfail.doc: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference' (Locked): 'Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls.' specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin' (Locked): 'A native pin MUST be a checked assertion over the complete transitive graph. Compilation MUST fail if any reachable operation or provider requires TypeScript. The diagnostic SHOULD show the dependency path that introduced the requirement.' Neither sentence makes reachability depend on how the callee's parameter is TYPED, and `run(new Widener())` really runs `Widener#read`.

notes: The shape is the whole point: `run`'s parameter is an interface, so the signature a checker selects for `reader.read()` is a member with no body, and an analysis that walks only the selected signature enters nothing and certifies the program. Reaching the body needs the other question — which VALUE arrives at the call — and the composed route is the evidence that it was asked. `messageContains` declares the whole tail rather than the code alone, because a pin refused with an EMPTY route satisfies a code-and-position expectation exactly; the fragment names the callee's module AND the method that ran, so a route that stopped at `run` fails this case even though it would carry the right code at the right position. `eval` is the corpus's existing `TypeScript` contributor (18-typescript-requirement and 21-native-pin/a-pin-reaching-typescript-is-rejected pin the classification independently), chosen so that the pin's diagnostic is the only one in the program and the route is the entire content of the expectation. The negative direction of this rule is pinned next door by 21-native-pin/a-callback-a-callee-only-stores-still-satisfies-the-pin, which must compile and run: a class instance handed to a callee that never calls anything on it is not part of the graph either.
